prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t honestly name one single “best” company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your house, budget, timing, system needs, and the crew you feel comfortable with. Instead, here’s a quick, practical way to find the best HVAC company in Atlanta for your AC replacement, plus what to watch for and an offer to help narrow options for your exact location.

How to find the best contractor
- Get 3 in‑home estimates. Prices and recommendations can vary significantly once the tech sees your system, ducts and attic.
- Verify credentials: ask for proof of insurance, EPA 608 certification (for refrigerant work), and any local/municipal licenses required where your home is located.
- Look for NATE‑certified technicians (good sign of training) and manufacturer dealer status for the brands they install.
- Check reviews on Google, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor and the BBB. Read recent reviews for consistency.
- Confirm they do a Manual J load calculation (proper sizing), and will address ductwork if needed.
- Ask about permits — the company should pull required permits and arrange inspections.
- Compare written estimates that show equipment make/model/SEER, scope of work, labor warranty, equipment warranty, tax and permit costs, and removal of old equipment.

Key questions to ask each contractor
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see proof?
- Do you have NATE‑certified techs?
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and inspect/measure ductwork?
- What brand/model are you recommending and why? (ask about SEER/EER)
- What’s included in the price? Any potential extra charges?
- How long is the labor warranty? What about the manufacturer warranty?
- Do you pull permits and handle inspections?
- Do you offer financing or rebates?
- Can you provide local references from similar jobs?

Red flags to avoid
- Very low bids with pressure to sign immediately.
- No written estimate or vague scope.
- Contractor unwilling to pull permits or provide proof of insurance.
- No references or mostly unresolved customer complaints.
- Rushing through the assessment without checking ducts or doing a Manual J.

Typical cost ranges (approximate)
- Central AC replacement in Atlanta: roughly $4,000 to $12,000+ depending on system size, brand, SEER rating, and whether ductwork needs repair or replacement.
- High‑efficiency systems or full duct replacement can push costs toward $10–15k or more.
(These are broad estimates — get in‑home quotes for accurate pricing.)

If you want, I can:
- Narrow down reputable companies near you if you tell me your ZIP code and any brand preferences.
- Provide a printable checklist or an email template you can use to request quotes and compare estimates.

Tell me your ZIP code and any priorities (budget, brand, timeline) and I’ll put together a short list of local contractors and what to ask them.
